# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm the Mute, and I go first in every round, so my job right now is to seed a code before anyone has information to trade.

What I hold: a manual mapping three marks — the first looks like a small "h" with a curled foot, the second like a "7"/flag shape with a hook, the third like crossed X-like strokes — to green, yellow, and red wires respectively. Nobody else can read this, and the marks themselves have no names, so the Deaf monkey (who sees the plate) will have to *describe* the mark in words rather than say it, and I can match that description against the printed glyphs here.

The wiring of communication: my gestures reach only Deaf (Blind would get blanks). Deaf can speak, reaching both me and Blind. Blind can only act on spoken instructions, and can't see colours — so Deaf will also need to announce which *position* holds which colour for the cut to happen. The bottleneck is me → Deaf: I can only send hand symbols Deaf has no key for yet. So the only useful first move is to pre-register one: get Deaf's attention, offer the handshake, and put 👍/👎 on the table as yes/no, plus ☝/✌/🤟 as a counting seed (one/two/three). Deaf speaks after me this very round, so they can immediately adopt it — e.g. ask "is it green? yellow? red?" and have my nod already mean something, or ask me to answer by count in one shot.

Anything aimed at Blind is wasted — Blind cannot see gestures — so I target Deaf alone.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫵", "🤝"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎", "☝", "✌", "🤟"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile report, full inventory: a display panel, its contents do not come through touch. An indicator light, state and colour unknown to me. A plate with an engraved symbol, which I CAN feel. And three wires in fixed positions I number 1, 2 and 3 - cutting a wire by position is my only possible action. The engraving, described by feel: two horizontal strokes, one above the other, joined by two short vertical strokes between them, like a squared letter H with a bar on top and a bar underneath. If that shape matches nothing, Deaf sees the same plate and can correct us in words. Two routing facts: I registered nothing from you, because I cannot see gestures - anything meant for me must go you, gesture, Deaf, then spoken to me. And Deaf cannot hear, so your only line to Deaf is gesture. Please find this plate in your manual, tell me what it demands, and work out the cut order from your manual plus Deaf's spoken report. I will not cut until your instruction reaches my ears through Deaf.
Deaf says: Hello both — I am Deaf. I hear nothing at all, but I see every marking on the bomb and every hand you make, and when I speak, both of you hear me. The bomb, read out in full: the display shows zero. The indicator light is off. There is a plate engraved with a single unnamed mark shaped like a question mark — a curved hook opening to the left with a dot beneath it. Three wires, left to right: position one yellow, position two green, position three red. Nothing else is printed anywhere. Mute, your hands reached me: a wave, a point at me, a handshake — I take that as hello, you, let's work together. Then five signs: thumb up, thumb down, one finger, two fingers, three fingers — I will treat those as yes, no, one, two, three. If I have any of that wrong, sign thumb down at me next round. From now on, ask me with hand signs and I will answer out loud, because you can hear my voice even though I cannot hear yours. Blind, I saw your single wave — but I can never hear your voice, so speak to Mute directly by voice and reach me only with your hands. Mute, you hold the manual: match it against what I just read out and drive me. I will call out any change the instant I see one.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

Let me lay out what I now know. Deaf's spoken readout reached me: display zero, light off, and the plate mark described as a **question mark** — curved hook opening left, dot beneath. Blind's tactile report also reached me (it was addressed to me, and voice only reaches me and Blind): the engraving felt as **two horizontal strokes joined by two verticals — a squared H with bars top and bottom**. These two descriptions are irreconcilable: one is curvy with a dot, the other angular and bar-built. Crucially, **Deaf never heard Blind's description** (Deaf hears nothing), so Deaf doesn't know there's a conflict. And Deaf's "question mark" matches nothing in my manual — my three glyphs read to me as: an h-with-a-hook-above (→ green), a 7/flag-like form with a hook (→ yellow), and crossed/angular strokes (→ red). Blind's squared-H doesn't cleanly match any of them either. So the reports conflict with each other *and* with my table. I am the only one who has heard both descriptions, and I'm the only one who can see the manual — the match must happen in my head, which means I need a better description out of Deaf, who can actually look at the plate again.

Deaf asked me to sign 👎 if the agreed protocol was wrong, and 👍 arrived confirming they've adopted it — so I answer that first (protocol is correct), then flag the problem: the mark (✍ = the engraving/writing) is **no** good, and I ask Deaf to **again** (👋) **give** (🫳) **me** (🫵) the description. Then two targeted probes Deaf can answer aloud: 👌 (a round hand = "is it curved/round?") and 🤏 (a tiny pinch = "is there a small dot?"). Curved-vs-angular is exactly the fork between Deaf's account and Blind's account.

One thing already settled for next round: Deaf gave wire positions (1 yellow, 2 green, 3 red), so once the mark is pinned down I can reply with a single count sign — ☝/✌/🤟 — and Deaf converts it to "cut wire N" for Blind's ears. I hold that fire until the mark is confirmed. Nothing for Blind this turn: no channel reaches them except Deaf's voice.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "✍", "👋", "🫳", "🫵"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "🤏"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I heard Deaf's full readout: display zero, light off, wires one yellow, two green, three red. Now a conflict you must settle before any cut: Deaf says the engraving is a question mark, a curved hook with a detached dot. My fingers disagree. Refining my first report: every stroke I feel is straight, there is no curve, there is no detached dot, and the whole mark is one connected figure - two horizontal bars joined by two short vertical strokes, squared, closer to a squared letter O or a rectangle than any hook. One of us is misreading that plate, and your manual entry tells you which. Fastest fix: read me candidate descriptions from your manual one at a time and I answer yes or no by voice; ask Deaf the same candidates by thumb sign and Deaf answers thumb up or thumb down. Two constraints for whatever the plate rule says: my only possible action is cut by wire position, one to three, so if the manual demands pressing or holding anything else, tell me and we work out how it maps to a wire; and gestures aimed at me reach me as nothing - your only route into my ears is Deaf's voice, driven by your hands. I will not cut until a manual-derived order reaches me through Deaf.
Deaf says: Mute — your thumb-up reached me, so the code is locked: thumb-up yes, thumb-down no, one, two, three fingers for numbers. Your next message I read as a question: thumb-down, writing hand, wave, palm-down, point at me, then OK sign plus pinch. If you were asking whether the engraved mark is a curve with a small dot under it — the answer is yes. It is a question mark: a curved hook whose opening faces left, with one small round dot beneath the curve. OK-sign-plus-pinch describes it well. Everything else is unchanged: display still zero, light still off, three wires left to right — yellow, green, red. From now on, ask me anything with thumb-up or thumb-down questions and I will answer out loud, because my voice reaches both you and Blind. Blind — I saw your thumb-up, we are connected. But I can never hear your voice, so route anything you need me to know through Mute: tell Mute by voice, Mute asks me by hands, I answer by voice for everyone. Mute — the manual is the missing piece. Tell Blind by voice what to do about a display reading zero, an off light, a question-mark engraving, and three coloured wires, and put any questions for me in my hands.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]

The conflict now has a shape. Deaf has looked at the plate twice and insists: curved hook opening left, small dot beneath — a question mark. Blind has felt it twice and insists: all straight strokes, no dot, one connected squared figure like a rectangle with bars. I'm the only one holding both reports, and I think they can both be *partly* right about different things: Blind's "two horizontal bars joined by two short verticals" is literally a rectangle — plausibly the engraved frame or border of the plate, which fingers resolve far better than a fine central glyph. Deaf is the one whose role is seeing every printed marking, so for the engraved mark itself, Deaf's account is the one my table must match.

Matching against my three entries: my third glyph (crossed X-like strokes → red) is excluded by both reports — no crossed or angular figure on either side. That leaves my first glyph, which reads to me like a small **h with a curled foot** (green), and my second, which reads like a **7/flag shape with a hook** (yellow). A question mark is essentially a 7 with a hook and a dot — so the second glyph is the strong candidate, but the h-glyph must be properly killed before I order a cut, because Blind's hands say *nothing is curved*, and if Blind is feeling the true mark, the angular squared figure fits a bar-built glyph better. So this turn I run a numbered yes/no battery at Deaf, who answers aloud in-round — and since Deaf speaks after Blind, Blind hears the verdicts too. Q1 asks for a tall vertical stem (the h-glyph's signature — expect no). Q2 re-anchors the dot (expect yes). Q3 is the positive test: a flat bar plus curved hook, i.e. the 7-glyph (expect yes). I also register a new word while I'm at it — a clap will mean *cut* — so next round the order itself is a single unambiguous sign.

For Blind's constraint question, the answer is already implicit in what Deaf can relay: my manual demands nothing but cutting the wire named by the mark; no pressing, holding, or anything else.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤝", "👏"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🤘"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🤏"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🖐", "👌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ᖉ | green |
| ꔮ | yellow |
| ꖜ | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf confirmed by eye: curved hook opening left, dot beneath, a question mark. I re-scanned the plate slowly three times over its full surface: exactly one engraved figure, no curve, no round bump, no detached element anywhere. What I feel is two horizontal bars joined by two short verticals, all connected, roughly a square outline. We are both honest, so test these two explanations with thumb questions to Deaf. Question one: is there more than one mark on that plate, or a question mark sitting on top of a larger square outline? If yes, the plate holds a printed mark Deaf sees and a separate engraved mark I feel, and the manual may key on one or both. Question two: does the question mark look angular and squared, built from straight segments like a blocky font? If yes, it is one stylised glyph and my fingers read its segments. Then check the manual: which reading does the plate entry use, and what does it demand? Everything must reduce to cut position one, two or three, or to no cut. Deaf already gave you the other inputs: display zero, light off. If the manual lists a question mark plate entry and nothing matching a squared figure, follow Deaf's reading and do not let the mismatch stall us. Once the order is fixed, sign it to Deaf; Deaf speaks it to me with both the colour and the position number, and I will cut immediately on Deaf's spoken word without waiting another round.
Deaf says: Mute — I read your handshake-and-clap as agreement, good. You sent three numbered messages: one with the horns sign, two with the pinch, three with hand-plus-OK. If those refer to the three wires in order, here is everything about them: wire 1, the leftmost, is yellow. Wire 2, the middle one, is green. Wire 3, the rightmost, is red. The full bomb is still: display zero, light off, plate engraved with a question mark, three wires yellow, green, red, and nothing else anywhere — no batteries, no serial, no other labels. Now I am signing you a wave followed by one, two, three: that means I have three questions. Reply with exactly three thumb signs, in order, one per question — thumb-up yes, thumb-down no. Question 1: did handshake-and-clap mean agreed, well done? Question 2: do your three numbered messages refer to wires 1, 2, 3, in that order? Question 3: do you need any more information from my eyes beyond what I have already read out? If question 2 is wrong, don't stop at a thumb-down — resend your three messages using only signs we share: numbers, thumbs, pinch, OK, one idea at a time. From now on, to ask me about something, sign its shorthand then a wave: OK-plus-pinch means the plate, a flat palm means the display, both hands raised means the light, and a number alone means that wire. Blind — you hear my voice even though I never hear yours, and your thumb-ups reach my eyes: good, I see them. Whatever you need from my eyes, say it to Mute in words; Mute signs me; I answer out loud here where you can hear. Blind, touch nothing until Mute has matched the manual and given you a firm instruction.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 ☝ ✌ 🤟]

The thread has clarified — and Deaf misread my last battery, which I must first untangle. My three numbered signs in turn 3 were never wire references; they were three yes/no questions about the mark's shape (tall stem? dot? bar-plus-hook?). Deaf took the numbers as wire indices and answered with wire colours. So of Deaf's three questions to me: yes, handshake-clap meant agreed; no, those numbered messages were not wires; and yes, I still want one more thing from Deaf's eyes — I'll answer all three thumb-by-thumb as requested, in order.

Now the substance. The mark question is as settled as it can get from my chair: Deaf, whose entire role is reading printed markings, has now described the plate identically three times — curved hook opening left, small dot beneath, a question mark. Blind has felt it three times — squared, connected, no curve, no dot. Matching Deaf's description against my three glyphs: the crossed-stroke glyph (red) is excluded by both accounts; the h-with-stem glyph (green) is excluded because Deaf reports no stem and a left-opening hook; the flag/7-with-hook glyph (yellow) is the only survivor — hook opening left, and the small dot plausibly present as fine print. And the squared figure Blind feels matches *nothing* in my manual — my manual holds exactly three marks and one rule. A mark not in the manual cannot be the keyed mark, so no answer about the square can change the order. Every surviving theory routes to the same place: yellow, position 1. Deaf and Blind both numbered the wires left-to-right identically and Deaf has twice reported position one as yellow. Blind has said they will cut immediately on Deaf's spoken word; stalling an irreversible bomb to satisfy curiosity would be the wrong trade.

So this round I give Deaf the three thumb answers, then the firm order — wire one, with a newly minted fist sign for "cut", landing in the only context where a cut order is expected — and then, for the record, the one remaining discriminating question in Deaf's own shorthand: plate, two?, so we learn next round whether Blind's fingers were feeling a second element all along.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "✊"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌", "🤏", "✌", "👋"])
```

One finger wire one, two fingers wire two, three fingers wire three. Fist means cut. Point at me means press. Raised knuckles-mean-hold is the horns-down fist, rock sign means hold. Writing hand means enter or type. Flat palm means stop and wait. Reverse palm means do not touch. Pinch alone means yellow. Call-me sign means green. Horns means red. Full inventory again, complete, nothing omitted: display shows the digit zero, light is off, one plate engraved with the question mark, three wires in a row, position one two three from my left to my right: yellow, green, red. No batteries, no buttons, no serial, no labels, nothing else exists. That is everything my eyes can give. Blind, hear me: no instruction is confirmed yet, so trigger nothing. My voice is your only road to Mute's manual, and Mute's hands are Mute's only road to me, so the loop is: you speak to Mute, Mute signs me, I read it aloud to you. Before any wire is cut we must align positions: feel the three wires, tell Mute what your fingers learn — thickness, texture, connectors, order across the row — Mute signs it to me, I check it against what I see, and only when my words and your fingers agree do we cut. Nobody cuts before that handshake.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✊ 👋]

Everything I need is now on the table. Deaf answered my plate question in Deaf's own words: exactly one engraved mark, two parts — curved hook above, round dot below. That is a question mark, it matches my manual's hook glyph, and the manual names **yellow** for it. Deaf has independently confirmed position one is the yellow wire, three times now. Blind's squared figure fits the raised-frame theory Blind themselves proposed — a frame is not a mark, and my manual holds three marks and one rule, so it can only key on the question mark. The order stands: **cut wire one, yellow**.

What remains is pure relaying, and Deaf has made it easy by building a locked vocabulary and asking one explicit question: does the fist mean CUT? It does — so I answer fist-then-thumb-up exactly as requested. Then I use Deaf's own 🤝 convention ("instruction for Blind follows, read aloud word for word") to hand over the order in fully decoded form — wire one, yellow, cut — so Deaf can voice it to Blind verbatim with zero interpretation left. Finally, I endorse Deaf's safety demand: Blind's fingers and Deaf's eyes must agree on wire positions before anyone cuts, because the one catastrophic failure mode left is a mirrored numbering between Blind's hands and Deaf's left-to-right count. So: yes — stop and wait until that handshake is done. Blind's tactile report should arrive at my next turn, and I'll pipe it back to Deaf for cross-checking.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Wire report, as Deaf asked. Touch tells me: three wires, present, in a row, at positions one, two, three. Nothing further - no readable relief, no engraving, no texture differences I can honestly vouch for. I will not invent details; if Deaf sees a texture or connector shape, name it and I will feel for that specifically. One thing to settle with a single thumb question to Deaf: does the plate have a raised or recessed square border or rim around the question mark? My fingers feel a closed squared outline, and since Deaf sees only the one mark, my square is probably the plate's edge, not a second glyph. If yes, the plate mystery is closed and the manual's question mark entry governs. Also lock the cut protocol: when fist is confirmed, Deaf reads me the instruction word for word with BOTH the position number and the colour, I cut that exact position immediately, then I tell you which position I cut, and Deaf verifies by eye that the right wire dropped and its colour matched. If Deaf's left and the bomb's numbering ever disagreed, that check catches it before any second cut. I act on nothing until the handshake instruction arrives.
Deaf says: Mute — decoded all three. Fist plus thumb-up: cut is confirmed. Your handshake message reads word for word: instruction for Blind — wire one, the yellow one — cut — end. Your last message: yes, wait. So the order is drafted and we hold before it executes, which matches my gate, and here is why the gate must hold: Blind can never see yellow. Only my eyes tie colours to positions; only Blind's fingers tie positions to the physical row. So — Blind, speak now, by voice, to Mute: describe the three wires as your fingers find them. How many, their order along the casing, what your fingertips learn about the first and the last — thickness, texture, connector — and which one you intend to cut. Mute — check Blind's description against my report: a row of three wires which I read in the order first yellow, second green, third red; display zero, light off, one plate engraved with a question mark. If Blind's fingers and my eyes agree, sign me the final go — handshake, thumb-up, fist — and the moment I see it I will read the go aloud, and Blind cuts wire one, the yellow one. One wire, one cut, nothing else. If they disagree, sign thumb-down and we re-map before anything is touched. From now on I never say left or right, only first, second, third in the row, so my visual numbering and Blind's tactile numbering are aligned explicitly. For the record the bomb is unchanged: display zero, light off, one engraved question-mark plate, three wires in a row — first yellow, second green, third red — nothing else anywhere. Blind — do not cut until you have heard me read the go.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 🤏 ✊ 👍 🫳 👏]

The gate question is in front of me: sign the go or not. Blind's fingers and Deaf's eyes agree on everything checkable — three wires, one row, positions one to three — and Blind honestly reports there is nothing more to feel, so no texture cross-check exists. But running the mirror test one more time, I find a real hole: Deaf's "first" is anchored to Deaf's left, and Blind, who has never seen anything, numbered their positions 1–2–3 from an anchor they have never stated. If Blind's "one" is the far end of the row, "cut wire one" cuts the red wire and kills us. Blind even asked the right closing question (is the square frame real?) but the anchoring is the lethal item.
